title: Understanding the Loss Function
text:
The loss function is defined as the residuals of the model. For a single observation, it is given by:

$$L(theta)=y_i-\operatorname{f_{	heta}}\left(x_iight)$$

This means the loss is the difference between the actual value $$y_i$$ and the predicted value $$\operatorname{f_{	heta}}\left(x_iight)$$.

title: Model Function
text:
The model function is given by:

$$\operatorname{f_{	heta}}\left(xight)=0.5	heta_0+	heta_0 	heta_1 x_1+sin\left(	heta_1ight) x_2$$

This function is used to predict the value based on the parameters $$	heta_0$$ and $$	heta_1$$.

title: Gradient Descent Update Rule
text:
The gradient descent update rule for parameters is:

(theta_0**(t+1),theta_1**(t+1))=(theta_0**(t),theta_1**(t))-(A,B)

Where A and B are the partial derivatives of the loss function with respect to $$	heta_0$$ and $$	heta_1$$, respectively.

title: Calculate A
text: To find A, we need to calculate the partial derivative of the loss function with respect to $$\theta_0$$. Start by substituting the model function into the loss function and then differentiate with respect to $$\theta_0$$.
